data.narrative:
Ethos Space is a seed-stage stealth company in Space & Aerospace, founded by Brogan BamBrogan, Jeff Overbeek, and Ross Centers. The sector contains a modest comp universe of 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though direct comparables at the seed stage are sparse.

Standard valuation triangulation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median analysis cannot proceed because no same-stage or adjacent-stage peers exist within a defensible filter—while 11 same-sector peers exist broadly, none meet minimum thresholds of three datapoints at comparable stage or valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring, though the Space & Aerospace sector shows a median price-to-sales multiple of 23.9x across six traded companies, cannot be deployed because the target's revenue is not on file; private frontier companies rarely disclose revenue at stealth stage, making top-line multiples inaccessible.

The lack of disclosed fundraising amount, current valuation, and operating metrics prevents quantitative synthesis. Without revenue, headcount, or previous round pricing, conventional methods yield no supportable range. Any valuation must await either disclosure of revenue and comparable recent private rounds in early-stage aerospace, or progression to a stage where such data becomes available. The analysis supports only the finding that standard VC triangulation is not yet feasible.
